## Glossary

**beginTurn**  
Durable acceptance of a turn before it runs: 409 on a duplicate, 503 if it cannot be made durable, 202 to the caller.

**core-thread**  
Class: core Thread, SessionManager blueprints, ownership scope, ids, and the persisted thread and message models.

**FoundryClient**  
Client for the daemon's loopback HTTP API, the same routes the viewer uses; refuses redirects, keeps the bearer on origin.

**idAtTime / timeFromId**  
Synthesize a UUID v7 for a cutoff date for id range queries / read the creation time back out of an id.

**isOpenTurn**  
Tells whether a turn status is accepted but not yet settled.

**Message**  
Prisma model: Postgres conversation rows grouped by turnId; not the local session store.

**newId**  
Mints a time-sortable UUID v7 id, optionally prefixed (newId('thr')); the id carries its creation time.

**normalizeScope**  
Copies an ownership scope dropping undefined fields, for stable equality.

**One turn path**  
Viewer, ACP hosts and Oracle runs share TurnService.accept → SerializedQueue → Harness.send; the viewer is not an ACP client.

**POST /api/messages/send**  
Accepts a turn with 202; the reply arrives on the thread:<id> stream, not in the response body.

**POST /api/threads/:threadId/turns/:turnId/interrupt**  
The stop route the viewer and ACP share (TurnService.interrupt); Codex has no native stop.

**Project / ProjectRegistry**  
A repo directory owning its threads, runtime adapter and tags / the lookup of every project by path or tag.

**renameThread**  
Viewer action setting a person's name on a thread, or handing naming back to the agent with an empty name.

**SerializedQueue (per thread)**  
A busy thread queues its next turn; a cancel before start never dispatches (CANCELLED_BEFORE_START).

**SessionManager**  
Holds the tree of threads; resolve / dispatch spawn a missing thread lazily from a registered blueprint.

**SessionManager.addBlueprint**  
Registers a match (string or RegExp) and create function that spawns threads for unknown destinations.

**SessionManager.inheritLayers**  
Builds a child thread's stack from the parent's layers: share (same instance) or copy (snapshot).

**splitHostInstructions**  
Separates the user's words from a host's wrapper text in a prompt (null if there is no wrapper).

**Thread**  
Core orchestrator for one unit of work: owns the context stack, agents, middleware dispatch, signal bus and status.

**Thread.dispatch**  
The single entry every host's turn passes through into flow middleware, the journal and InjectionArtifact.

**thread.fan()**  
Dispatches one payload to several agents in one thread with allSettled; returns FanResult[] per agent.

**ThreadFactory**  
Builds a new isolated Thread from the project template, cloning warm layers and agents per thread.

**ThreadNamer**  
Keeps an agent-maintained short name on each thread after completed turns, off the turn path.

**ThreadRuntimeManager**  
Attaches and disposes a live thread's runtime: Librarian, Wardens, flow, sinks, bindings.

**threads**  
Class: the thread runtime and the one turn path (TurnService, queued turns, projects, ThreadFactory, ThreadRuntimeManager, FoundryClient).

**ThreadState**  
Prisma model: thread metadata only (description, tags, status, parent, archive time).

**threadTitle**  
Picks the title a thread shows: a person's name over the agent's.

**TurnService**  
The one turn lifecycle: accept, queue, dispatch, stream and settle, behind POST /api/messages and every host.

## 1. What this Warden covers

The thread as Foundry's unit of work and the one path every turn takes through it: how a thread is built, found, given a live runtime, named and stored, how every host's turn is accepted, queued, dispatched and settled, and the time-ordered ids every record uses.

## 2. The domain

A core Thread owns one unit of work: its context stack, registered agents, middleware dispatch (Thread.dispatch), signal bus and metadata (describe / tag / archive); thread.fan() sends one payload to several agents with allSettled, so one failure does not kill the rest. In Foundry, ThreadFactory builds a new isolated Thread from the project template (cloning warm layers and agents), SessionManager holds the tree of threads and spawns a missing one lazily from a registered blueprint on resolve or dispatch (inheritLayers shares or copies the parent's layers), and ThreadRuntimeManager attaches and disposes the live runtime: Librarian, Wardens, flow, sinks and bindings. A Project is one repo directory owning its threads and runtime adapter; ProjectRegistry finds projects by path or tag.

Every turn, from the viewer, Zed, Paseo, T3 or an Oracle run, goes through TurnService: accept (beginTurn: 409 on a duplicate, 503 when not durable, 202 to the caller), the per-thread SerializedQueue (a busy thread queues; a cancel before start never dispatches), Harness.send, the flow and executor, then settle, with output appended on the thread:<id> stream. Never write a turn lifecycle inline in a route; stopping goes through the shared interrupt route. FoundryClient is the loopback client for CLI and host processes, using the same daemon routes as the viewer; the viewer's store actions (selectThread, revertThread, stopTurn, loadOlderMessages, renameThread) sit on those routes. ThreadNamer keeps an agent-maintained short name off the turn path, a person's name (renameThread) always wins, and threadTitle picks what is shown. Ids are UUID v7 from newId, so the id carries its time (timeFromId reads it, idAtTime turns a cutoff into an id comparison) and there are no created_at columns. Message and ThreadState are the Postgres rows (conversation rows by turnId; metadata only).

Not here: the local journal, phase rows, content-addressed records, subagent child threads and turn-end compaction are the `journal-thread-tree` region; what a native session receives each turn and its delivery ledger are `native-sessions`; ACP method mapping and session/update projection are `acp`; Wardens held inside the thread's own Claude process and its setup turn are `in-session-wardens`; when a Warden is asked is `warden-triggers`; the decision login and priority the naming call runs on are `decision-hosts`; the viewer's pages are `viewer`.

### 4a. Doc sections

Each unit is the doc section verbatim, with its headings shifted down two levels. A source line above it gives the path, the section and the doc's H1.

**Source:** `docs/reference/FOUNDRY-ACP.md` § 3. Dogfooding: one turn path (in "Headless Foundry over ACP")

#### 3. Dogfooding: one turn path

foundry-acp is the **second client of the daemon's API**, the one the viewer uses. The viewer does not become an ACP client:

1. **ACP is too narrow for the viewer.** The flow graph, phase journal, layers, traces, corrections, settings and Kingdom pairing have no ACP message. Routing them through ACP would be a private protocol inside `_meta`.
2. **The browser cannot be an ACP client.** ACP's transport is stdio; ACP over HTTP/WS is still experimental in the SDK.
3. **Gaps surface where they belong.** A gap foundry-acp hits is a gap the viewer has too (the missing stop route was one). Fixing it once fixes both.
4. **No new trust surface.** The proxy reaches the daemon over loopback, like the MCP bridge proxy.

**The one turn path.** A turn from Zed, Paseo, T3, the viewer or an Oracle run:

```
TurnService.accept             (beginTurn: 409 duplicate, 503 not durable; 202 to the caller)
  → per-thread SerializedQueue  (a busy thread queues; cancel before start never dispatches)
  → Harness.send               (pc/harness.ts:277)
  → classify ∥ route ∥ flow.prepare (early start, pf/agents/thread-runtime.ts:905-915)
  → flow-pre-message           (preMessage → hydrateDelta; route/advice phase rows sealed before the executor, :930-988)
  → Executor → SessionBackedProvider → HarnessSession.send (native preflight, admission, interruptible)
  → commitDelivery, postAction guards, Warden review (unchanged)
  → thread:<id> appends and the sender's terminal → viewer tab   and   → foundry-acp → session/update
```

ACP-originated threads are ordinary threads, so the viewer shows them live: flow graph, journal, corrections.

<!-- unit doc:docs/api/PRIMITIVES.md#thread -->
**Source:** `docs/api/PRIMITIVES.md` § Thread (in "Foundry Primitives — API Reference")

#### Thread

Orchestrator. Owns stack, agents, middleware, signals.

```ts
import { Thread } from "@foundry/agent-primitives";

const thread = new Thread("main", stack, {
  description: "Main conversation",
  tags: ["feature-auth"],
  maxDispatches: 10000,
});

thread.register(classifier);
thread.register(router);
thread.register(executor);

// Dispatch (runs through middleware chain)
const result = await thread.dispatch("classifier", payload, filterOverride?);

// Fan out (allSettled — partial failures don't kill the rest)
const results = await thread.fan(["agent-1", "agent-2"], payload);
// returns FanResult[] with { agentId, status: "fulfilled"|"rejected", result?, error? }

// Metadata
thread.describe("Working on auth refactor");
thread.tag("auth", "security");
thread.archive();

thread.meta  // { description, tags, status, createdAt, lastActiveAt }
```

<!-- unit doc:docs/api/PRIMITIVES.md#sessions -->
**Source:** `docs/api/PRIMITIVES.md` § Sessions (in "Foundry Primitives — API Reference")

#### Sessions

Lazy thread resolution. Router says "send to X" — if X doesn't exist, it's created.

```ts
import { SessionManager } from "@foundry/agent-primitives";

const sessions = new SessionManager();
sessions.add(mainThread);

// Register blueprints for lazy creation
sessions.addBlueprint({
  match: /^feature-.*/,  // String or RegExp
  async create(destinationId, parent) {
    const childStack = SessionManager.inheritLayers(parent!, {
      share: ["docs"],          // Same layer instance
      copy: ["conventions"],    // Snapshot copy
    });
    const child = new Thread(destinationId, childStack, {
      description: `Feature thread: ${destinationId}`,
    });
    child.register(makeExecutor(destinationId));
    return child;
  },
});

// Resolve — finds existing or spawns from blueprint
const thread = await sessions.resolve("feature-auth", mainThread);

// Dispatch across threads
await sessions.dispatch("feature-auth", payload, {
  sourceThread: mainThread,
  agentId: "executor",
});

// Tree
sessions.parentOf("feature-auth")   // → mainThread
sessions.childrenOf("main")         // → [feature-auth thread]
sessions.active                     // non-archived threads
sessions.archived                   // archived threads
```

### 4b. Code entries

From the catalog (extracted from the code through the repo's Atlas map, described by a model). Each line: **name** `where` [kind] the job it does. Use: canonical usage.

#### Class `threads`
- **FoundryClient** `packages/foundry/src/client/foundry-client.ts#FoundryClient` [primitive] call the daemon's loopback HTTP API with the same routes the viewer uses Use: new FoundryClient(endpoint).<route>()
- **isOpenTurn** `packages/foundry/src/persistence/local-session-store.ts#isOpenTurn` [primitive] tell whether a turn is accepted but not yet settled Use: isOpenTurn(status)
- **loadOlderMessages** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/ui/store.js#loadOlderMessages` [primitive] fetch the next older page of a thread's messages Use: await loadOlderMessages(threadId)
- **Project** `packages/foundry/src/agents/project.ts#Project` [primitive] represent one repo directory that owns its threads, runtime adapter and tags Use: new Project(config) // via ProjectRegistry.register(path)
- **ProjectRegistry** `packages/foundry/src/agents/project.ts#ProjectRegistry` [primitive] look up, filter by tag and serialize every project this Foundry instance knows Use: registry.register(path); registry.get(id)
- **renameThread** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/ui/store.js#renameThread` [primitive] set a person's name on a thread, or hand naming back to the agent with an empty name Use: await renameThread(threadId, name)
- **revertThread** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/ui/store.js#revertThread` [primitive] rewind the active thread to a message index Use: await revertThread(messageIndex)
- **selectThread** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/ui/store.js#selectThread` [primitive] make a thread active by id and restore its messages Use: selectThread(threadId)
- **SessionManager** `packages/foundry/src/agents/session.ts#SessionManager` [primitive] hold the tree of threads and create missing ones lazily from a blueprint on dispatch Use: sessionManager.get(threadId) // spawns from blueprint if absent
- **splitHostInstructions** `packages/foundry/src/turns/host-instructions.ts#splitHostInstructions` [primitive] separate the user's words from host wrapper text in a prompt Use: splitHostInstructions(prompt) // null if no wrapper
- **stopTurn** `packages/foundry/src/viewer/ui/store.js#stopTurn` [primitive] interrupt a queued or running turn through the interrupt route Use: await stopTurn(threadId, turnId)
- **ThreadFactory** `packages/foundry/src/agents/thread-factory.ts#ThreadFactory` [primitive] create isolated Threads from the project template with per-thread layers and agents Use: threadFactory.create(...) // clones warm layers and agents per thread
- **ThreadNamer** `packages/foundry/src/agents/thread-namer.ts#ThreadNamer` [primitive] keep an agent-maintained short name on each thread, off the turn path Use: new ThreadNamer(...) // runs after completed turns
- **ThreadRuntimeManager** `packages/foundry/src/agents/thread-runtime.ts#ThreadRuntimeManager` [primitive] attach and tear down each live thread's runtime (Librarian, Wardens, flow, sinks, bindings) Use: runtimeManager.attach(thread) / dispose(threadId)
- **TurnService** `packages/foundry/src/turns/turn-service.ts#TurnService` [primitive] run the one turn lifecycle: accept, dispatch, stream and settle for sync and streamed routes Use: turnService.<accept/run>(...) // behind POST /api/messages

#### Class `core-thread`
- **Message** `prisma/schema.prisma` [model] store every row produced inside a thread turn, grouped by turnId Use: prisma.message.findMany({ where: { threadId }, orderBy: { id: 'asc' } })
- **ThreadState** `prisma/schema.prisma` [model] persist a snapshot of thread metadata: description, tags, status, parent, archive time Use: prisma.threadState.upsert({ where: { id }, create, update })
- **idAtTime** `packages/core/src/id.ts#idAtTime` [primitive] synthesize a UUID v7 for a point in time for id range queries by age Use: idAtTime(prefix, cutoffDate)
- **newId** `packages/core/src/id.ts#newId` [primitive] mint a time-sortable UUID v7 id, optionally prefixed Use: newId('thr')
- **normalizeScope** `packages/core/src/scope.ts#normalizeScope` [primitive] copy an ownership scope dropping undefined fields for stable equality Use: normalizeScope(scope)
- **Thread** `packages/core/src/thread.ts#Thread` [primitive] own the context stack, agents, middleware dispatch, signal bus and status of one unit of work Use: new Thread(...)
- **threadTitle** `packages/core/src/thread.ts#threadTitle` [primitive] pick the title a thread shows, a person's name over the agent's Use: threadTitle(meta)
- **timeFromId** `packages/core/src/id.ts#timeFromId` [primitive] read the millisecond creation time out of a UUID v7 id Use: timeFromId(id)
